verdict: The Gamer Xtreme with an RTX 3050 is about the least you can spend on a new prebuilt that still has a real graphics card. Listings usually pair the card with a recent Intel Core i5, 16 GB of memory and an NVMe SSD, which is a sensible base: the CPU is strong enough that a much faster graphics card can go in later without the processor holding it back.

The weak point is the RTX 3050 itself. It handles Fortnite, Valorant, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League and Minecraft at 1080p, but new AAA games need medium or low settings, and the 6 GB version is noticeably slower than the 8 GB card. Independent reviews put an RTX 5060 roughly twice as fast, so this machine makes most sense when the budget is truly fixed near $700.

Two things decide whether a specific listing is a good buy. Check that the memory is two sticks rather than one, because single-channel memory costs frame rate in CPU-heavy games, and check the power supply's wattage and brand so you know whether an RTX 5060-class upgrade will be possible. If the price climbs past about $800, the [iBuyPower Slate with an RTX 4060](/gear/ibuypower-slate-rtx-4060/) is the better buy.

faqs.q: Can the CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme with an RTX 3050 run Fortnite?
faqs.a: Yes. An RTX 3050 runs Fortnite comfortably at 1080p with performance-focused settings, and esports titles like Valorant and Counter-Strike 2 run at high frame rates. New AAA games need medium or low settings.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 3050 6GB or 8GB better?
faqs.a: The 8 GB version is clearly better. The 6 GB RTX 3050 has fewer cores and less memory bandwidth as well as less VRAM, so independent reviews put it well behind the 8 GB card. Check the listing title before buying.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade the graphics card later?
faqs.a: Usually yes, as long as the power supply has the wattage and connectors the new card needs. Check the PSU wattage in the listing; an RTX 5060-class card is the most common upgrade for this kind of system.

verdict: The Slate with an RTX 4060 is a solid 1080p machine. The [RTX 4060](/gear/rtx-4060/) runs most current games at 1080p high settings, and DLSS 3 frame generation helps in the games that support it. Independent reviews put it roughly level with an RTX 3060 Ti in raster at 1080p, with much lower power draw, so it is easy on the power supply and quiet in a small case.

Its limit is the 8 GB of VRAM, which already forces texture settings down in some new releases, and the card is being replaced by the RTX 5060, which is somewhat faster for similar money. If you find a Slate with an RTX 5060 near the same price, take that one. iBuyPower uses standard desktop parts, so upgrading the graphics card or adding storage later is straightforward.

verdict: The Omen 16L is HP's small gaming desktop, and in an RTX 5060 configuration it delivers the same 1080p high-settings performance as other RTX 5060 systems. Its appeal is the package: a compact case that fits on or under a desk, HP's warranty and support, and availability at big-box stores where you can return it easily.

The cost is flexibility. HP uses its own motherboard and power supply designs in the Omen line, and a compact case limits the size of a future graphics card. Owners report that upgrading the GPU or power supply can be harder than in a standard tower, so if you expect to swap major parts, the [Skytech Archangel](/gear/skytech-archangel-rtx-5060/) or [iBuyPower Slate](/gear/ibuypower-slate-rtx-4060/) is the better base.

Prices swing a lot with HP's frequent sales, and the Omen 16L is only good value toward the bottom of its range. Configurations also vary in CPU, memory and storage, so compare the exact specification against an RTX 5060 tower before buying.
pros: Easy to find and return at retail

faqs.q: Is CyberPowerPC a good brand?
faqs.a: CyberPowerPC is one of the biggest US system builders. Most buyers report good experiences, with complaints mostly about shipping damage and unbranded parts on some listings. Check the power supply and inspect the PC when it arrives.

faqs.q: Gamer Supreme or Gamer Xtreme?
faqs.a: The Gamer Supreme is CyberPowerPC's higher-end line, with faster GPUs and often liquid cooling; the Gamer Xtreme covers budget and mid-range builds. Compare the actual parts, since both names cover many configurations.

faqs.q: Does the Gamer Supreme come with Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Many listings include Wi-Fi, but not all. Check the specification table for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth before you buy if the PC will not be near your router.

name: Alienware Aurora (RTX 5080)
description: The Alienware Aurora with an RTX 5080 is a $2,500 to $3,000 4K gaming desktop with Dell's support. You pay a premium, and Dell's case limits some upgrades.
quick: Dell's Alienware Aurora gaming desktop in an RTX 5080 configuration. It targets 4K and high-refresh 1440p, with Dell's warranty and support network behind it.
bestFor: 4K gamers who value Dell's support and a polished, quiet case over the lowest price
skipIf: You want the most performance per dollar; system-builder RTX 5080 PCs usually cost less
specs: Dell unit; wattage varies by configuration
Dell limited warranty; check the listing
verdict: The Aurora with an RTX 5080 is built for 4K and high-refresh 1440p. The [RTX 5080](/gear/rtx-5080/) is NVIDIA's second-fastest card and, with DLSS 4, handles demanding games at 4K. Alienware's case is designed for quiet running, and Dell's warranty and support options are the strongest reason to choose it over a system-builder PC.

You pay for that. Alienware desktops usually cost more than an RTX 5080 system from Skytech, CyberPowerPC or iBuyPower with similar parts, and Dell uses some of its own components and case layouts, so owners report upgrades can be less flexible than in a standard ATX tower. Watch for Dell's frequent sales, which can close much of the gap.

Because RTX 5080 systems are expensive, check the CPU carefully: for the highest frame rates, a Ryzen 7 9800X3D or a current Core Ultra 7 or 9 is what this card deserves. Compare the [RTX 5080 against the RTX 5070 Ti](/compare/rtx-5080-vs-rtx-5070-ti/) too, since the cheaper card is close at 1440p.

extra.heading: What to Check in the Listing
body: Prebuilt configurations change from listing to listing, sometimes under the same product name. Before you buy, confirm five things in the specification table: the exact graphics card model and its VRAM, the CPU model, whether memory is installed as two sticks (dual channel) or one, the SSD capacity, and the power supply's wattage and brand.

If the power supply is listed only by wattage with no brand or 80 Plus rating, treat that as a reason to ask the seller or pick another listing. See our [power supply guide](/best-power-supply/) for what a good unit looks like, and the [PSU calculator](/tools/psu-calculator/) for the wattage a later GPU upgrade would need.

faqs.q: Is the Alienware Aurora worth it?
faqs.a: It is worth it if you value Dell's support and a polished case. On raw performance per dollar, RTX 5080 systems from Skytech, CyberPowerPC or iBuyPower usually cost less.

faqs.q: Can the Alienware Aurora run 4K?
faqs.a: Yes. With an RTX 5080 it runs demanding games at 4K, using DLSS 4 in the heaviest titles. The RTX 5080 has 16 GB of VRAM.

faqs.q: Can you upgrade an Alienware Aurora?
faqs.a: Memory and storage are straightforward. Graphics card and power supply upgrades depend on the case and Dell's power supply; check card length and wattage before buying.

quick: Corsair's AMD-based Vengeance a8200 gaming PC in an RTX 5080 configuration. Corsair builds it largely from its own power supply, memory, cooling and case.
bestFor: 4K gamers who want a premium prebuilt with named power supply, memory and cooling
skipIf: Price per frame matters most; an RTX 5070 Ti system is close at 1440p for much less
specs: Corsair unit; wattage varies by configuration
Corsair liquid cooling in many configurations
verdict: The Vengeance a8200 is Corsair's AMD-based gaming PC, and its strength is the parts list. Corsair makes power supplies, memory, coolers, SSDs and cases, so a Vengeance system is built largely from named Corsair components rather than unbranded ones. That is the main reason to pay its premium over a system-builder RTX 5080 PC.

With an [RTX 5080](/gear/rtx-5080/), it is a 4K machine: demanding games run well at 4K with DLSS 4, and high-refresh 1440p is easy. If the configuration uses an X3D Ryzen such as the [Ryzen 7 9800X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-9800x3d/), it is also one of the fastest gaming CPU pairings available.

The case is a standard design with good airflow, so upgrades are easier than in most brand-name desktops. The cost is price: expect to pay more than for a Skytech or CyberPowerPC RTX 5080 system with similar headline specs. If 1440p is your target, the [Skytech Azure 3 with an RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/skytech-azure-3-rtx-5070-ti/) gets close for roughly $900 less.

faqs.q: Is the Corsair Vengeance a8200 good?
faqs.a: Yes, if you value named parts: Corsair builds it from its own power supply, memory and cooling. With an RTX 5080 it is a 4K gaming PC, though it costs more than system-builder equivalents.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Vengeance a8200 and i7600?
faqs.a: The a in the name marks an AMD Ryzen platform and the i an Intel platform. Check the exact CPU and graphics card in each listing, since both names cover several configurations.

faqs.q: Is an RTX 5080 PC worth it over an RTX 5070 Ti PC?
faqs.a: For 4K, often yes. At 1440p the RTX 5070 Ti is close in independent reviews and its systems cost several hundred dollars less, so it is the better value there.
